subject: Response-time churn affecting BrightCart — coordination & customer message
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Response-time churn affecting BrightCart — preliminary notes

Team —

Monitoring flagged repeated p95/p99 response-time churn on BrightCart's gen-api routes starting ~13:40 PDT. Impacted endpoints are /v1/generate (streaming) and /v1/embed for a narrow subset of keys tied to the account. Early indicators:
- p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.6s in short bursts (see attached incident_timeline.csv).
- Spike correlates with several large fan-out requests and a small number of long-history chat sessions causing KV cache thrash on a handful of GPU nodes.
- No full node OOMs reported; CPU on proxy tier spiked briefly.

Immediate ask: 1) SRE to confirm if KV eviction pattern matches the timeline and whether warmup can be accelerated; 2) Product to weigh in on safe temporary routing change (pinning to lower-memory model variant) and whether we can enable a short-lived per-customer fanout throttle; 3) Sales/CS to approve tone of customer note below before I send it.

Draft customer note attached in cust_note_draft.docx; quick summary below when we respond: apology, what we saw, short-term mitigations (routing + throttling), and timeline for follow-up including long-term product ask (KV warmup improvements + cache sizing guidance).

Thanks — Mateo

Mateo Alvarez
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Response-time churn affecting BrightCart — preliminary notes

On 2027-03-25 14:02, Mateo Alvarez wrote:
> Monitoring flagged repeated p95/p99 response-time churn on BrightCart's gen-api routes starting ~13:40 PDT.

Quick triage: I pulled traces for the affected shard set. Two observations:
- We see repeated KV misses for sessions with >6k token histories; those calls hit the same GPU group and cause sequential cache loads.
- Some requests are arriving in short bursts (burstiness from their side). The runtime serializes heavy KV reloads which increases tail.

Immediate mitigation idea (SRE + product): temporary policy to route sessions with histories >4k tokens to a variant with smaller KV footprint (quantized model v2-q4) for 30m while SRE applies a KV-prewarm experiment.

I will attach a short timeline and sample traces. Karthik — can you confirm if we can safely prewarm the affected KV ranges without risk of additional pressure?

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Response-time churn affecting BrightCart — preliminary notes

Marissa — good call on the routing option. Quick technical note from SRE:
- KV eviction correlates with a wave of concurrent long-history requests that cause continuous cache churn on two GPU pods (g-14 and g-17). Eviction rate spiked at 13:41 and persisted in pulses until 13:56.
- We can run a targeted KV prewarm for the top 200 session keys identified in the timeline; prewarm should complete in ~90s but will allocate additional GPU memory while running. That is safe for a single pod at a time.
- Alternative: apply a short-lived routing rule to divert sessions with token_count > 4000 to v2-q4 on the next routing sync; this is the least invasive and avoids pod-level memory rebalancing.

Asks:
1) Product (Soojin) — can you sign off on enabling the routing rule for BrightCart for 30 minutes and add a temporary flag so we can revert automatically?
2) Product — prioritize a small KV warmup API (internal flag) we can flip per-customer during rolling restarts; we can prototype in the next sprint but need a short-term workaround.

I'll open INF-9123 with the traces and start the prewarm job against g-14 as a controlled test. Marcus — please coordinate CS language for the customer note.

Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Response-time churn affecting BrightCart — preliminary notes

Thanks — I approve the routing rule for a 30-minute window with automatic revert. Two quick product asks I want documented as follow-ups:
- KV warmup API: small product ticket to expose an internal flag to prefetch KV ranges by session id(s). Scope: internal-only, opt-in per customer, low-risk memory allocation guardrails.
- Quantization/variant guidance: create a short-runbook recommending model variants for high-history workloads and a recommended token threshold for routing.

I'll add both to the roadmap backlog and file PRDs: one immediate low-effort instrument (flag + automated revert) and one medium-term spec (warmup API + monitoring).

Soojin

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart Platform Team <platform@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-26T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Brief update: response-time instability earlier today (13:40–13:56 PDT)

Elena —

Thanks again for flagging the tail latency you observed earlier. Quick update on what we found and immediate next steps:

What happened (short):
- Between 13:40–13:56 PDT a small subset of BrightCart requests with very long session histories caused repeated cache evictions on two GPU pods, which increased p95/p99 for a portion of traffic. There was no data loss and no request failures — just increased response times.

What we did (short-term mitigations):
- We applied a temporary routing rule for 30 minutes to route very long-history sessions to a lighter-weight model variant while we validated a targeted KV prewarm on affected pods.
- SRE ran a controlled prewarm on the impacted GPU pod; cache hit-rate returned to baseline after the operation.

Next steps (what we're doing for you):
- We will deliver a post-incident summary with timelines and sample traces by EOD today (Jira INF-9123).
- Product is prioritizing an internal KV-warmup mechanism and a short runbook recommending model variants for long-history sessions. We will share expected ETA for the warmup capability in our follow-up.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min technical readout with your platform team to walk the traces — let me know availability. Apologies for the disruption; we know predictable latency is critical.

Best —
Mateo
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
